main_text.p: Sed prohibitus à multitudine, cujus voluntas ipsi ignota non erat (magnam enim partem confiliorum confciam, ac patratorum scelerum participem habebat) & retinere potestatem rogatus, sic demum assensit, si sine collegis imperium sibi tenere liceret. Dicebat, grave sibi fore, eorum quæ collegæ committerent, id quod lex juberet, rationem reddere. Cui cum adstipulata concio esset, confestim designatus fuit strategus αὐτοκράτως [?]. A quo tempore curis omnibus reipublicæ in se receptis jam sine contradictione dominatum tenuit, aliis præ metu necessitati parentibus, aliis mutatione ipsa lætis, multis, qui tenui in re erant, largitionum spe acquiescentibus. Nam in concione novas tabulas dispungendorum nominum, & agrorum divisionem Agathocles promiserat. His ita constitutis velut repente mutatus, missis cædibus & injuriis benignum ac facilem se omnibus dedit, multos beneficiis, alios promissis sibi devinxit, humanus, affabilis, in tantâ potentiâ nec diadema sumpsit, nec custodiâ corporis more aliorum dominantium se muniit. Reliqua, quæ ad tuendum imperium pertinebant, struendis ac reficiendis longis navibus, parandis arm[?][illegible, ~2 letters][illegible, ~3 letters][illegible, ~2 letters]

page.notes: The first line is cut off at the top of the scan, so "Sed" may continue from the previous page; it is marked cont="true" on that basis. The final word "arm" is cut off by the bottom edge of the scan; "armis" is likely but not legible, hence [?]. The Greek word after "strategus" is hard to read at this resolution; the form αὐτοκράτως is my best reading and should be checked against the scan, since the printed form may be αὐτοκράτωρ. Right margin notes are only partly visible, cut off by the scan edge, and could not be read; their positions are marked approximately. The two lines at the bottom right are partly visible and unreadable; they may be show-through from the reverse side. Left margin shows only small marks and no readable text.
